answers.question: Does the ping break his alibi?
answers.text: If the ping is accurate, it seriously undercuts his alibi. He swore he never left the Westside Diner between 9:30 and 11:00 PM, but the Tower 4 records place his phone at Pier 9 at 10:14 PM. That doesn't prove he was at Pier 9, though. It shows where the phone was, not who was holding it, and tower pings only give a rough area. Whether it breaks the alibi depends on how precise that location is and whether anyone else had the phone.

answers.question: How precisely can a Tower 4 ping locate a phone?
answers.text: A single tower ping gives an area, not a pin-point. Accuracy depends on how densely towers are spaced: in cities it may narrow things to a few blocks or one sector, while a rural tower can cover a radius of 30 km or more. The episode says the Tower 4 records place Marcus Vance's phone at Pier 9 at 10:14 PM, but it hasn't said how far Tower 4 is from Pier 9 or how the location was narrowed, so the exact precision is still unknown. The ping supports his presence in that tower's coverage area, not that he was at Pier 9 specifically.

answers.question: Who had the access to cut the harbor cameras?
answers.text: The episode so far doesn't say who had access to cut the harbor cameras. It only says the cameras were "deliberately severed" moments after Vance's phone pinged at Pier 9, which places him on the pier at that time but doesn't show who cut the cameras. The access question is still open, so we'll need to wait for later evidence.

answers.text: The transcript so far doesn't mention a burner phone being smashed, or any time it was destroyed. The only phone detail is that Tower 4 cell dump records put Vance's phone at Pier 9 at 10:14 PM. That doesn't yet show whether he had a second phone or what happened to it.
